The QCEW provides industry-level wage data, while CPS unionization rates can be merged by industry code to test the conditional effect.

[PATH:literature] Borjas (2003) 'The Labor Demand Curve Is Downward Sloping' and subsequent meta-analyses on immigration and wages — This foundational study and its critiques (e.g., Ottaviano & Peri, 2012) provide theoretical frameworks and empirical benchmarks. Reviewing whether unionization moderates the wage effect is a known gap; a meta-regression of existing studies that include industry-level union density could refute or support the hypothesized interaction.

[PATH:theoretical] Simulated structural model of labor market with union wage-setting and low-skill immigration — A computational model incorporating union bargaining power (e.g., right-to-manage or efficient bargaining) can generate counterfactual wage effects under varying unionization rates. This would test the logical consistency of the hypothesis and identify conditions under which the effect might be amplified or nullified, guiding empirical specification.
